topic: || vs ??: || replaces every falsy value including 0 and empty string, ?? only replaces null and undefined (MDN)
text:
A quantity of 0 turned into 42. The bug is one operator.

`||` returns the right side for any falsy left side: 0, "", NaN, false. MDN warns this causes surprises when those are valid values.

`??` only falls back on null or undefined:

const count = 0;
count || 42; // 42
count ?? 42; // 0

Settings, counters, prices and empty-string inputs are exactly where this bites. A user who sets volume to 0 gets your default instead.

Rule of thumb: use `??` for defaults, and `||` only when you really want every falsy value replaced.

Have you ever shipped a default that overrode a valid 0 or empty string?
